_note: B-31. License levers on the mock tenant's licenses family file (fixtures/tenant/<client>/licenses.json). Mock only; no real tenant or vendor portal is called. Free stock only: nothing here buys a seat (W-VND-02 is never automated; a lever named license.purchase* cannot load).

levers.name: license.add
levers.description: Give one user a license from a seat the client already owns. With no free seat it proposes nothing and says a purchase needs the client's consent. Mock of a license assignment.

upn.description: userPrincipalName of the user to license

sku.description: SKU part number the client already owns, e.g. O365_BUSINESS_ESSENTIALS

impact.L1: A new hire can open mail and Office on day one; a wrong SKU gives them more or less than their job needs until it is changed.
impact.L2: The client's seat count goes up by one inside what it already pays for; no money is spent and no contract changes.
impact.L3: Licensing a new hire stops being a ticket that waits on a person to check seats; every assignment is a registered, approved and audited change, and a shortage is reported, not bought around.
impact.L4: Seats are counted per client, so one office's free seats are never given to another's; a shortage goes to the client as a decision for them, not a cost they find on a bill.

levers.name: license.remove
levers.description: Take a license from an offboarded user once the retention window has ended; the diff shows the SKU and the date the window ended. Mock of a license removal.

sku.description: SKU part number to remove, e.g. O365_BUSINESS_PREMIUM

impact.L1: A departed person's license ends after the agreed retention period; a wrong removal can be undone only while a free seat is left, and data tied to the license may be affected.
impact.L2: The client stops paying for seats nobody uses and a seat is free again for the next hire; a removal before the window is over would cut access to data they meant to keep.
impact.L3: Forgotten removals stop costing clients money for months; the lever refuses inside the window and each removal is approved and audited, showing the SKU and the date the window ended.
impact.L4: Seat counts shown to a client match what it really uses, so the bill is honest; a removal acts on one client's own licenses only.
